params.body:
The network graph on **Netwerk** was a fixed picture: dense in the middle, labels on top of each other, nothing to pull apart. It now moves:

- **Drag a dot** and the dots it shares projects with follow. A dragged dot stays where it was put, so clusters can be laid out by hand at the table. **Schudden** lets every dot go and settles the picture again.
- **Drag the background** to move the whole; **scroll** or **pinch** to zoom, around the pointer or between the fingers. Buttons for **+**, **-** and **Passend** (everything in view).
- **A tap** still opens the relation. Hovering a dot shows its name and projects.
- Labels keep their size on screen at any zoom, and more of them appear as you zoom in.
- Positions, zoom and the dots placed by hand are kept while the page redraws, so tagging a relation no longer throws the picture around.

Still a small simulation of its own in `resources/js/network-graph.js` (repulsion, springs weighted by shared projects, a pull to the middle, damping), with pointer events for mouse and touch alike. No new package, nothing new in the content policy.

This branch is built on #61, so it contains that change too: merge #61 first, or merge this one and close #61.

Checked in a browser against a local database with a made-up network: dragging moves a dot and it stays, a tap opens the relation, scrolling zooms, the graph survives a redraw. `NetworkTest` passes. The full suite was not run again for this change (JavaScript and one view only).
params.title: Netwerk: drag, pan and zoom the graph
